name: Log Size Ratio of Singletons
details: The value is zero at $n=2$ and tends to one as $n\to\infty$. The asymptotic classification concerns sufficiently large $n$.
proof: The singleton class has $n$ concepts on an ambient domain of size $n$. For $n\ge2$, substitution in the definition gives $\log(n-1)/\log(n+1)$. At $n=1$ there is one concept, so the numerator would be $\log 0$ and the real-valued ratio is undefined. At $n=2$ the numerator is zero. Dividing numerator and denominator by $\log n$ shows that the ratio tends to one.
